g.text: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a compelling alternative
to autoregressive models, offering advantages such as parallel generation,
bidirectional context, and natural controllability (Ye et al., 2025; Nie et
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=3) Diffusion language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a compelling alternative to autoregressive models, offering advantages such as parallel generation, bidirectional context, and natural controllability (Ye et al., 2025; Nie et al., 2025; Sahoo et al., 2024).

g.text: However, their iterative denoising process creates significant inference
overhead: each of the hundreds of diffusion steps requires a forward pass
over the full sequence, making deployment computationally expensive.
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) However, their iterative denoising process creates significant inference overhead: each of the hundreds of diffusion steps requires a forward pass over the full sequence, making deployment computationally expensive.

g.text: Window-Diffusion (Zuo et al., 2026) addresses this by restricting attention
to a sliding window around the decoding frontier, achieving substantial
speedups while largely preserving generation quality.
g.title: N3 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) Window-Diffusion (Zuo et al., 2026) addresses this by restricting attention to a sliding window around the decoding frontier, achieving substantial speedups while largely preserving generation quality.

g.text: However, Window-Diffusion couples two distinct operations at each
phase boundary: (1) shifting the window to align with the current
decoding frontier, and (2) performing a full KV cache refresh.
g.title: N4 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, Window-Diffusion couples two distinct operations at each phase boundary: (1) shifting the window to align with the current decoding frontier, and (2) performing a full KV cache refresh.

g.text: A single refresh cycle parameter controls both frequencies, creating an
efficiency trade-off: shifting windows more often improves quality but
g.title: N5 [Limitation] (cites=0) A single refresh cycle parameter controls both frequencies, creating an efficiency trade-off: shifting windows more often improves quality but forces more expensive full refreshes.

g.text: We observe that these two operations serve fundamentally different
g.title: N6 [Method] (cites=0) We observe that these two operations serve fundamentally different purposes and can be decoupled.

g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) We propose Overlap-Refresh, which introduces two independent scheduling parameters: shift interval controls how often the window moves, while refresh interval controls how often full KV recomputation occurs.

g.text: At shift-only boundaries, we use delta-prefill—computing KV only
for newly entered tokens while reusing cached KV for overlap
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=0) At shift-only boundaries, we use delta-prefill—computing KV only for newly entered tokens while reusing cached KV for overlap tokens.

g.text: This achieves O(|N | × C) cost versus O(C 2 ) for full refresh, where |N |

g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We identify the coupling inefficiency in Window-Diffusion's phase boundary operations and show that naive refresh reduction degrades both quality and speed.

g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose Overlap-Refresh, which decouples window shift frequency from KV refresh frequency via two independent scheduling parameters.
